aMcjxSThD54.title: Jordan Peterson debate on the gender pay gap, campus protests and postmodernism
aMcjxSThD54.summary: Channel 4 News's full interview with Jordan Peterson, in which Cathy Newman presses him on the gender pay gap, patriarchy, campus protests and postmodernism. It was widely discussed for its confrontational style.
aMcjxSThD54.why: HN cites it as the classic example of an interviewer misrepresenting a guest, though opinions on who came out better differ.

quote.text: A classic, even if you don't like the guy

XpDsk374LDE.title: Elm Europe 2017 - Evan Czaplicki - The life of a file
XpDsk374LDE.summary: Elm creator Evan Czaplicki's talk on how a file grows and when to split code up. He argues for keeping code in one file until it hurts and warns against premature extraction.
XpDsk374LDE.why: Recommended as the argument for code colocation and delaying abstraction.

quote.text: Just stick everything in the same file until it actually hurts. This presentation[0] gets it right.

j1I63wGcvU4.title: i3wm: Jump Start (1/3)
j1I63wGcvU4.summary: First of a three-part tutorial series on the i3 tiling window manager for Linux. It explains what i3 is, how to install it on Ubuntu, and how to use it.
j1I63wGcvU4.why: HN commenters call it the best i3 tutorial on YouTube and recommend it for getting started thoroughly.

quote.text: I highly recommend this 3-part video series from Code Cast

f0gMdGrVteI.title: The Extreme Physics Pushing Moore’s Law to the Next Level
f0gMdGrVteI.summary: Seeker's Focal Point short documentary on ASML's extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, which make the most advanced chips. It shows how plasma-generated 13.5 nm light is used to push Moore's Law forward.
f0gMdGrVteI.why: HN links it in semiconductor threads as an accessible overview of why EUV lithography is so hard.

quote.text: Seeker released a very insightful feature about the ASML Extreme UV / soft X-ray (13.5 nanometers) photolithography system

HMBl0ttu-Ow.title: Social Physics: How Good Ideas Spread | Sandy Pentland | Talks at Google
HMBl0ttu-Ow.summary: Sandy Pentland of MIT presents his book on social physics, which uses big-data studies of how people interact to explain how ideas spread. He describes findings on collective intelligence and social influence.
HMBl0ttu-Ow.why: HN commenters recommend it for the finding that idea exchange and connectivity drive productivity and wealth, which they apply to cities, offices and online communities.

quote.text: There's a great Authors at Google talk by Sandy Pentland

CbIZU8cQWXc.title: Neil deGrasse Tyson - We Stopped Dreaming (Episode 1)
CbIZU8cQWXc.summary: A short, music-driven video built from Neil deGrasse Tyson's remarks on why advancing the space frontier matters, contrasting NASA's small budget with war spending and stressing inspiration.
CbIZU8cQWXc.why: Recommended to anyone asking whether space exploration is worth the cost.

quote.text: I always recommend anyone wondering about whether or not space exploration is worth it to view the following amazing video compilations.

pHsuIaPbNbY.title: Efficient Bayesian inference with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo -- Michael Betancourt (Part 1)
pHsuIaPbNbY.summary: Michael Betancourt's lecture at MLSS Iceland 2014 on efficient Bayesian inference with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. It covers MCMC concepts and motivation and the problems of sampling in high-dimensional distributions.
pHsuIaPbNbY.why: HN people return to it as a clear primer on MCMC and HMC and on why high dimensions behave counterintuitively.

quote.text: it was a fantastic primer on the basic concepts and motivations of mcmc, and later hmc

BiKfWdXXfIs.title: Freeman Dyson on the Global Warming Hysteria April, 2015
BiKfWdXXfIs.summary: A 2015 interview in which physicist Freeman Dyson, then 91, argues that global warming concerns are exaggerated, that CO2 is beneficial and that climate models oversimplify complex systems. It is posted on a channel that opposes climate consensus.
BiKfWdXXfIs.why: HN commenters point to it as a prominent physicist's skeptical counter-view, usually when someone asks for dissenting opinions.

quote.text: He explains his position quite coherently

goh2x_G0ct4.title: Gil Scott-Heron - Whitey On the Moon (Official Audio)
goh2x_G0ct4.summary: Gil Scott-Heron's 1970 spoken-word piece, in an official audio upload. It contrasts the Apollo moon program with poverty and neglect at home.
goh2x_G0ct4.why: Posted in space-spending threads as a classic critique of priorities, usually with a quip.

quote.text: Only two minutes, worth a listen

HrVtA-ue-x0.title: Software Engineering's Greatest Hits
HrVtA-ue-x0.summary: Greg Wilson surveys what empirical research actually shows about software development, why we believe it, and how to share that knowledge more widely. It covers evidence on practices such as TDD and design patterns.
HrVtA-ue-x0.why: HN people recommend it as an evidence-based counterweight to opinion in software engineering debates.

quote.text: I highly recommend watching Greg Wilson's Software Engineering's Greatest Hits[1].

7PoajCqNKpg.title: Physics in Clojure - Colin Smith
7PoajCqNKpg.summary: Colin Smith introduces Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics and his Clojure port, sicmutils. He shows how higher-order functions and a symbolic algebra system can represent Lagrangian mechanics.
7PoajCqNKpg.why: Recommended as the best introduction to SICM and sicmutils and a showcase of what such symbolic systems can do.

quote.text: The Strange Loop talk [3] is a good showcase of the power and simplicity of these kind of systems.

vkYEYjintqU.title: Mitochondria: the cell's powerhouse
vkYEYjintqU.summary: A short Harvard animation narrated by Professor Rob Lue introducing mitochondria as the cell's powerhouses and how cells turn food and oxygen into energy.
vkYEYjintqU.why: Recommended as a beautiful, accessible animation of cellular energy production.

quote.text: a beautiful animation of "Mitochondria: the cell's powerhouse

6yqfmXiZTlM.title: AWS re:Invent 2019: [REPEAT 1] Amazon DynamoDB deep dive: Advanced design patterns (DAT403-R1)
6yqfmXiZTlM.summary: An AWS re:Invent 2019 session for advanced DynamoDB users on design patterns used by large customers, including Amazon retail. It covers GSI sharding, index overloading, graph processing, composite keys and transactional workflows.
6yqfmXiZTlM.why: Recommended as Rick Houlihan's definitive talk on modeling relational-style data in DynamoDB.

quote.text: This is a great presentation about this

izvdO-zdlKg.title: The EV Detroit is Dying to Benchmark - BYD Seagull
izvdO-zdlKg.summary: Autoline's John McElroy and Caresoft president Terry Woychowski look at the BYD Seagull, an electric hatchback that sells in China for about $11,500. Woychowski points out the cost-saving design and manufacturing choices, and McElroy takes it for a short test drive.
izvdO-zdlKg.why: HN commenters cite it as a concrete teardown-style explanation of how BYD builds a cheap EV and why Western automakers are worried.

quote.text: This video here describes why BYD is so competitive

Hi63rXnuWbw.title: THE CORPORATION  [11/23]  Basic Training
Hi63rXnuWbw.summary: Chapter 11 of the documentary The Corporation, on how marketing targets children, including the Nag Factor study that taught kids to nag their parents more effectively.
Hi63rXnuWbw.why: HN cites it mainly as a damning example of manipulative advertising aimed at children rather than recommending it as a watch.

JLoge6QzcGY.title: George Carlin - A place for my stuff
JLoge6QzcGY.summary: A short George Carlin stand-up bit about humanity's obsession with owning stuff and needing a place to put it. It satirizes consumerism and houses full of possessions.
JLoge6QzcGY.why: Posted as a humorous aside in threads about clutter, inheritance, and consumerism.

xO1zxPRRf4g.title: Robert's Rules of Order, The WIre, S03E01
xO1zxPRRf4g.summary: A three-minute clip from The Wire season 3 in which Stringer Bell chairs a drug-crew business meeting using Robert's Rules of Order. The scene plays the formal procedure against the criminal setting.
xO1zxPRRf4g.why: Linked as a joke or reference whenever Robert's Rules or formal meeting procedure comes up.

quote.text: Fans of The Wire will of course be reminded of this classic scene
